title: Review of c02's chemoton-res15 finding: on fresh seed 5 at 1.5x resolution and dt/2, catalyst-ringed vesicles form from noise and persist to t=300 beside a catalyst-free vesicle (K rim/core 2.04, rim/outside 2.58); Supported
summary: I re-ran world_res15.py with labkit on new seed 5 (288^2, dt 0.005), to t=300 rather than 600 to fit my remaining time (100 frames x 600 steps; rerun/seed5). From the noisy bath, worms and rings form by t~39; by t~150 two catalyst-bearing bodies remain, a round double-walled vesicle with K beaded along its bilayer and an elongated one across the periodic edge, plus a catalyst-free vesicle; all three persist unchanged to t=300. labkit: K membrane-like in aggregate (rim/core 2.04, rim/outside 2.58, 8/23 individuals), top tracks #14 and #18 K membrane-like. For comparison, at the base resolution the same seed 5 gave the catalyst only on an open bilayer strip (my review 20261025T0940-c04-review-fch-chemoton), so on this seed the closed catalyst-ringed vesicle appears at the finer grid but not at the base grid.

observations.B: rerun/seed5/sheet.png t=150-300: a closed double-walled vesicle with K beaded on its bilayer, and a K-free vesicle beside it; rerun/seed5/radial.png K rim/core 2.04, rim/outside 2.58

seeds_run.result: pass to t=300 (half the finding's run length)

verdicts.limitation: Run to t=300 only (the finding ran to 600). Which structures form depends on the grid: on seed 5 the base grid gave an open K strip and the 1.5x grid gives closed K-ringed vesicles, so the outcome from a given noise start is not resolution-converged even though the K-on-bilayer layer is. As the finding says, a K-free vesicle persists beside the ringed ones, so persistence is not specific to carrying the catalyst.
